diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof of the following result is identical to \Cref{lem:rep_in_time} and is omitted.

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's convention, the inverse DFT carries the factor 1/(length). For a signal of length dN this factor is 1/(dN). The d-fold periodic sum contributes a factor d when d divides n, so y_{dn} = (1/(dN))·d·Σ_k x̃_k e^{...} = x_n, not d·x_n. The time-domain proof of Lemma rep_in_time has no normalization factor, so it is not 'identical' to this case, and the second claim of the lemma is false as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the conclusion by y_{dn} = x_n and supply the short computation that includes the 1/(dN) normalization.
issues.overall_effect: The second assertion of the lemma is false. The subsignal derivation uses only the vanishing of y_j for j not a multiple of d, and its final display can be checked directly, so downstream results are unaffected.
issues.title: Frequency-repetition lemma states a wrong scaling factor and its omitted proof does not transfer
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction to an unused part of a lemma; no substantive result changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, set $m_j = j(k/d_1)^{-1}p \bmod{N_1}$ for the row index,

issues.failure_explanation: k/d1 is coprime to N1/d1 = D1, not necessarily to N1. For example, take N1 = 12 and k = 9. Then d1 = 3 and k/d1 = 3, but gcd(3,12) = 3, so 3 has no inverse modulo 12. The construction of m_j, and likewise n_j, is therefore undefined in general.

failure_location.quote: Since $d_1 = \gcd(k, N_1)$ and $d_2 = \gcd(l, N_2)$, $k/d_1$ and $l/d_2$ must have multiplicative inverses modulo $N_1$ and $N_2$, respectively.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take inverses modulo D1 and D2 instead. Then m_j(k/d1) ≡ jp (mod D1) gives m_j k ≡ jpd1 (mod N1), and the rest of the argument goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The existence step of the proof that every subsignal entry receives contributions is invalid as written. The lemma's conclusion and its uses in lem:amb2D remain repairable.
issues.title: False invertibility claim for k/d1 modulo N1 in the subsignal counting lemma
issues.why_classification: A one-line change of modulus restores the argument with no loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity gcd(pk,N1) = p·gcd(k,N1) requires p | D1, not merely p | N1. Take N1 = 4, N2 = 6 and (k,l) = (0,1), so D1 = 1, D2 = 6 and p = 2 divides N1. Then gcd(0,4) = 4, not 8, and D1/p = 1/2 is not an integer. The prerequisite (0,2)-subsignal is actually available through the other branch. The case split should be on p | D1 versus p ∤ D1.

failure_location.quote: If $p \divs N_1$, then $\gcd(pk, N_1) = p\gcd(k, N_1) = N_1/(D_1/p)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split the cases on p | D1 versus p ∤ D1. In the latter case p | D2, so D1 is unchanged and D2 decreases, and the argument then goes through as written.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification that all decimated subsignals are available before each ILP in Algorithm memo_2D is flawed. The ordering itself is still correct.
issues.title: Incorrect case split in the correctness argument for the DP iteration order
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of the case split fully restores the correctness argument; the algorithm is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The $60 \times 60$ matrix required $350 / 3600 \approx 9.7\%$ of DFT coefficients,
they were still inverted from a relatively smaller sampled spectrum than the $60 \times 60$ matrices.

issues.failure_explanation: Table tab:rect reports that reliable 11x13 recovery (M=5) used 16 coefficients, under the same counting that gives 350 for 60x60. That is 16/143 ≈ 11.2%, which exceeds the 9.7% for 60x60. The prose figure of 8/143 is inconsistent with the table, and the stated conclusion is reversed.

failure_location.quote: whereas the $11 \times 13$ matrix required $8 / 143 \approx 5.6\%$ of DFT coefficients for reliable inversion.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the fraction from Table tab:rect as 16/143 ≈ 11.2% and drop or reverse the comparative conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The empirical claim that 11x13 matrices were inverted from a smaller fraction of the spectrum than 60x60 matrices is not supported by the paper's own data.
issues.title: Sampling-fraction comparison for 11x13 contradicts the reported coefficient count
issues.why_classification: This is a side empirical remark; correcting it affects no theorem, algorithm or guarantee.
